reason: E2 shows that principal elements segregate to grain boundaries in HEAs and that brittle intermetallic phases can form there, but it does not demonstrate that fast nanosegregation alone (without intermetallic formation) causes embrittlement, nor does it provide evidence that preexisting Cr-rich precipitates can act as sinks to absorb segregants and improve ductility. E1 describes general embrittlement mechanisms but does not support the specific claim that precipitates mitigate segregation-induced decohesion. The core mechanistic premises are therefore largely unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Fast nanosegregation of principal elements (Ni, Cr, Mn) to grain boundaries occurs in single-phase HEAs at intermediate temperatures
This segregation reduces grain boundary cohesion and promotes intergranular cracking
Preexisting Cr-rich grain boundary precipitates can absorb embrittling segregants
Absorbing segregants into precipitates reduces their concentration at grain boundaries and mitigates decohesion
The engineered dual-phase alloy will therefore show higher ductility and less intergranular fracture than the single-phase baseline
